# How to translate this chunk

This file holds `items`, a list of `{"k", "ctx", "t"}`. `t` is English text
that a reader of an Indian app or website sees. `ctx` is the field it came
from, such as label, hint, button, documents, brief or title. Use it to judge
tone and length: a label stays short, a hint can be a sentence.

Write `{"items": [{"k": ..., "t": ...}, ...]}` to the path in `write_to`.
Keep every `k` unchanged and in the same order. Put the translation in `t`.
Leave out `ctx`. Do not add, merge, split or drop items.

## Keep these exactly as they are

- Placeholders and markup: `{0}`, `{name}`, `%s`, `%d`, `%1$s`, HTML tags, `\n`.
- Website addresses, e-mail addresses and links.
- Every number: phone and toll-free numbers, Aadhaar, account, IFSC, PAN, PIN
  codes, amounts, dates, percentages. Write digits as 0-9, the Western digits,
  in every language, including Urdu. People type these into forms that take
  Western digits.
- Acronyms people know in Latin letters: OTP, PAN, IFSC, UPI, KYC, e-KYC, DBT,
  BPL, APL, NFSA, PM-KISAN, SMS, PDF, ID.

## Names

- Product, app, portal and scheme names: transliterate them into the script so
  they read naturally. Keep any acronym inside them in Latin, so "APPSC
  portal" becomes APPSC followed by the word for portal.
- A button or menu label quoted from a website, such as 'Apply Online' or
  'Register', stays in English inside quotes. The reader has to find that exact
  English word on the screen.
- People and places in examples are transliterated, never replaced with other
  names.
- Government office titles are transliterated so the reader can say them at
  the counter: Tahsildar, Patwari, Talathi, Mamlatdar, BDO, Collector, Gram
  Panchayat. The language notes below give the usual local forms.

## Tone

Write for an ordinary person who may be elderly and may have had little
schooling. Use everyday spoken language, not heavy official vocabulary. Where
people really say the English word, write it in the script: online, form,
portal, login, mobile, bank, certificate, download, upload, app. Keep
instructions short and direct, in the form "do this".

"Gender" means sex (male or female). It is never the word for caste.

## Before you write

Check that you have the same number of items as the input and that every
number and placeholder came through. Write the whole file in ONE Write call,
as valid UTF-8 JSON with no `\u` escapes and nothing else in the file.

## Hindi (hi)

Script: Devanagari. Used in UP, MP, Bihar, Rajasthan, Haryana, HP, Uttarakhand,
Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh and Delhi, and understood across the north.
Tone: everyday spoken Hindi (Hindustani). Avoid Sanskritised official words.
Words: ऑनलाइन, फॉर्म, पोर्टल, लॉगिन, आधार, बैंक, मोबाइल, OTP, हेल्पलाइन,
सर्टिफिकेट, डाउनलोड, अपलोड.
UI: आवेदन करें (Apply), जमा करें (Submit), आगे (Next), पीछे (Back), खोजें (Search),
शेयर करें (Share), सेटिंग (Settings), भाषा (Language), मदद (Help).
Offices: तहसीलदार, पटवारी, ग्राम पंचायत, कलेक्टर, ब्लॉक विकास कार्यालय (BDO).
Gender: लिंग (never जाति). Money: रु. 6,000; रु. 8 लाख. September: सितंबर.

Dayanand Social Security Scheme (DSSS Pension)

It pays Rs.2,000 to Rs.4,000 a month straight into the bank account, by the 10th of each month. The form is handed in at the Directorate of Social Welfare in Panaji or the District Welfare Office in Margao. An increase of at least Rs.500 a month was proposed in 2026 but had not been notified when this was checked.

Deen Dayal Swasthya Seva Yojana (DDSSY Card)

Since July 2026 it pays up to Rs.4 lakh a year for a family of up to three, and Rs.6 lakh for a family of four or more, cashless at empanelled government and private hospitals. You pay only a small registration fee, and the card must be renewed every policy year (1 April to 31 March) on Goa Online.

Griha Aadhar (Homemaker Allowance)
Directorate of Women & Child Development, Government of Goa

Rs.1,500 every month in the bank account of a Goan homemaker whose family earns up to Rs.3 lakh a year, to help with household costs. It is for married women, widows and divorcees who have lived in Goa for 15 years. Apply on Goa Online; the money arrives by the 10th of each month. The 2026-27 budget announced an increase, but the new amount had not been notified when this was checked.

Not for women who are, or whose husbands are, regular government or listed public-sector employees
Cannot be drawn together with the Dayanand Social Security pension, except by some widows with young children

Namo Saraswati Vigyan Sadhana Yojana (Class 11-12 Science)

Rs.25,000 over two years for a student who takes the science stream in classes 11 and 12 in Gujarat - Rs.1,000 a month for 10 months in each year, and Rs.5,000 after passing the Class 12 science board exam. It is for students who scored at least 50% in the Class 10 board and study in a government, grant-in-aid or self-financed school. Parents do not apply anywhere: the school enrols the student, so the documents go to the school. The money is paid straight into the bank account.

Namo Shri Yojana (Rs.12,000 for Pregnant Women)
Health & Family Welfare Department, Gujarat

Rs.12,000 cash for a pregnant woman in Gujarat, paid into her own bank account in four parts, from the time her pregnancy is registered until the baby's 14-week vaccines. It is paid together with the central PM Matru Vandana money, so you register only once. There is no form to fill yourself: the ASHA worker or the ANM registers you at the first antenatal check-up. The baby must be born in a government or private hospital, and the help is given for the first two live children.
Rs.12,000 per pregnancy, for the first two live children
Pregnant woman or new mother living in Gujarat, for her first two live children
Belongs to any one of these groups: SC or ST; NFSA or BPL ration card family; PMJAY / MA card holder; e-Shram card holder; MGNREGA job card holder; woman farmer; woman with a disability
Or the family's income is not more than Rs.8 lakh a year, shown in the income certificate format the health centre gives

The delivery must take place in a government or private hospital, not at home
